title: SLI contract friction and cross-team learning sprint retrospective (Nov 2024)
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Overview:

This retrospective captures the outcomes from the two-week cross-team learning sprint (Nov 4–18, 2024) that emerged after multiple small but persistent SLI contract breaks across platform components. The goal of the sprint was to: (1) surface where SLI definitions and alert contracts diverged between teams, (2) produce concrete dashboard and alert changes that reduce noisy page wakes, and (3) update operator-facing runbooks to speed diagnosis.

Summary of findings:
- Multiple teams (allocator, prefetch-controller, router, kv-prefix-cache) had subtly different interpretations of the same SLIs (e.g., "token_cost_per_request" vs "token_cost_per_user_request").
- Alerts were firing during legitimate transient load patterns due to brittle burn-rate thresholds and missing context panels (tenant, region, model_variant).
- Operators lacked a compact decision canvas that maps an alert to the minimal triage checklist; this increased mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) by ~14 minutes for the incidents observed.

Why this matters:
- Repeated noisy wakes increase cognitive load on oncall, leading to escalation fatigue and slower response for customer-facing failures.
- Misaligned SLI semantics drive inefficient mitigations (over-provisioning, unnecessary rollbacks, customer-impacting throttles).

Sprint timeline and scope:
1) Nov 4–6: Discovery interviews with allocator, prefetch, routing, and telemetry teams.
2) Nov 7–10: Correlate alert history with token-cost and latency SLI graphs (historical window: Sep–Nov).
3) Nov 11–14: Implement dashboard prototypes and adjusted alert rules in staging.
4) Nov 15–18: Run operator tabletop exercises and collect feedback; finalize runbook edits.

Incident examples (representative) and impact:
- Incident A (2024-10-29): Prefetch-controller alert group fired repeatedly for burn_rate > 1.2 for 5m. Root cause: transient multi-tenant warmup spike combined with an alert that ignored tenant priority. Oncall paid ~28 minutes of hands-on investigation before demoting to monitoring-only.
- Incident B (2024-10-31): Router p95 foreground latency SLI breached (threshold 450ms p95). Alerts lacked model_variant context and routed to infra team instead of serving runtime — added 22 minutes of routing handoffs.

Root causes and evidence:
- SLI naming drift: teams stored token-cost metrics under different labels (token_cost.count, token_cost.request_sum, token_cost.user_request_sum). This caused dashboards and composite SLIs to disagree. Evidence: PromQL queries used by allocator (token_cost.request_sum / requests_total) vs prefetch (token_cost.count / user_requests_total).
- Alert burn-rate sensitivity: burn-rate thresholds tuned for sustained regressions (targeting 30–60 minute degradations) but applied at 5–10 minute windows by several legacy alerts.
- Missing contextual dimensions: most alerts did not include tenant_id, model_variant, or region tags, making it hard for oncall to determine blast radius.

Key dashboards and alert changes (deployed to staging Nov 12, promoted Nov 16):
- New composite panel: "Token cost per effective request (by tenant)"
  - Query (PromQL example): sum by (tenant_id) (increase(token_cost.request_sum[10m])) / sum by (tenant_id) (increase(requests_total[10m]))
  - Visualization: stacked area + table with top 25 tenants by cost delta.
- Alert rule: token-cost-gradual-burn
  - Old: burn_rate(token_cost.request_sum[5m]) > 1.2 for 3m
  - New: burn_rate(token_cost.request_sum[15m]) > 1.15 AND topk(3, increase(token_cost.request_sum[15m])) / increase(requests_total[15m]) > 1.1 for same tenants
  - Rationale: extend window to filter transients; only page when top tenants drive the change.
- Latency alert adjustment: router-p95-deg-guard
  - Old: p95(router_latency_ms)>450ms for 10m
  - New: p95(router_latency_ms{model_variant!="fallback"})>500ms for 15m AND increase(error_count[15m])>5
  - Rationale: ignore known fallback variants and require traffic-impact signal.

Runbook and operator-facing updates:
- New triage canvas (one-page) added to runbooks: "S3: Signal, Scope, Stabilize"
  - Signal: confirm metric delta and check burn-rate over 5/15/60m.
  - Scope: narrow to tenant/model_variant/region using dashboard drilldowns.
  - Stabilize: apply blue-green routing to target model_variant or enact tenant soft-quota; avoid immediate global rollbacks.
- Runbook snippet (shell helpers and queries):
  1) Quick tenant list: curl -s http://ops-api/internal/top-tenants?window=15m | jq '.'
  2) Prefetch warmset health: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=prefetch-controller -o wide
  3) Check KV prefix shard states: redis-cli -h kv-prefix-cache-01 INFO keyspace || redis-cli -h kv-prefix-cache-02 INFO keyspace

Operator tabletop outcomes and metrics:
- MTTA reduced from baseline 16.4m -> 9.8m in staged exercises (avg across 6 scenarios).
- False-positive page rate for token-cost alerts dropped ~62% in staging over two weeks.
- Operator confidence score (survey, n=12) increased from 2.6 -> 3.8 /5 for triage clarity.

Decisions and governance changes (approved Nov 18):
- All SLI definitions exposed in the shared telemetry repo must include canonical metric name, recommended aggregation window, primary dimensions (tenant_id, region, model_variant), and owner. (See Appendix: SLI metadata template).
- New "SLI change request" flow: small SLI changes may be approved by two owners (observability + affected service). Larger semantic changes require a 5-day notice and cross-team review.

Action item list (owners and ETA):
1) Telemetry team: publish canonical SLI metadata for token-cost, router-latency, and kv-read-latency. (Owner: Marta Gómez; ETA: 2024-12-05)
2) Prefetch team: add tenant-level breakdown panels to public platform dashboard. (Owner: Arjun Patel; ETA: 2024-12-12)
3) Observability: update alert library with burn-rate templates and parameterized examples. (Owner: Ethan Rodriguez; ETA: 2024-12-08)
4) Oncall: adopt the "S3 triage canvas" into weekly runbook training. (Owner: Liam Chen; ETA: 2025-01-15)
5) Platform product: document cost-aware routing fallback policies in the public operator guide. (Owner: Priya Natarajan; ETA: 2024-12-22)

Roadmap/Follow-ups for Q1 2025:
- Q1 sprint: SLI metadata registry (service: telemetry-sli-registry) with an API and a UI for cross-team discovery.
- Dashboards: template library of compact triage dashboards that can be instantiated per model_variant and tenant slice.
- Automated page suppression: short-term generator to gate burn-rate paging if the top-k metric contributor is a pre-approved maintenance window.

Lessons learned (concrete):
- Small differences in metric naming cause outsized operational friction; invest in canonicalization early.
- Burn-rate is an effective early-warning signal but must be tuned with windowing and contributor context to avoid noise.
- Operator training and a one-page triage canvas materially reduce cognitive load and response time.

Appendix A — SLI metadata template (example):
| field | example | notes |
|---|---|---|
| canonical_name | token_cost.per_request | metric namespace used in Prometheus |
| promql_example | sum by (tenant_id) (increase(token_cost.request_sum[15m])) / sum by (tenant_id) (increase(requests_total[15m])) | recommended query to compute SLI |
| aggregation_window | 15m | default window for burn-rate and smoothing |
| primary_dimensions | [tenant_id, model_variant, region] | required tags for dashboards/alerts |
| owner | team/telemetry | team responsible for correctness and migration |

Appendix B — Example alert YAML (operational template):
---
alert: token-cost-gradual-burn-template
expr: |
  sum by (tenant_id) (increase(token_cost.request_sum[15m])) / sum by (tenant_id) (increase(requests_total[15m])) > 1.1
for: 15m
labels:
  severity: warning
  team: platform-telemetry
annotations:
  summary: "Token cost per request rising for tenant {{ $labels.tenant_id }}"
  runbook: "https://confluence.internal/redwood/eng-platform/runbooks/s3-triage-canvas"

Appendix C — Owners matrix (compact):

- Prefetch: Arjun Patel (owner), Mei Lin (support)
- Router: Samir Desai (owner), Liam Chen (support)

Contact and next steps:
